Hi Sara —

Thanks for the log. I ran three compact scenarios in the attached workbook (redwood_long_history_example.xlsx) — pasted a short summary below. I kept the math explicit so procurement can map numbers to PO lines.

Scenario A — stateless long-prefix per-call (no KV cache reuse):
- Typical call: 30,000 prefix + 600 user tokens + 400 model tokens => raw = 31,000 tokens
- Per-request quantum: 100 tokens => rounded up to 31,100 tokens billed
- If you do 1,000 such calls/day => daily billable tokens = 31,100,000

Scenario B — persistent session, KV cache reuse of prefix (recommended):
- First call stores prefix in KV and bills full 30,000 + generation tokens. Subsequent calls only bill user + model tokens (e.g., 1,000 calls/day x (600+400)=1,000,000 raw tokens)
- With 100-token quantum rounding, overhead is ~100 tokens per request => 100,000 extra tokens/day instead of 31M. Big delta.

Scenario C — commit SKU with session minimums waived:
- For committed Dedicated/Dedicated-Reserve, we can set a per-session minimum (e.g., 500 tokens) and reduce per-request quantum to 10 tokens for long-running flows. This is something we can negotiate in the contract.

Other practical notes:
- We typically show both raw token and rounded-token columns on invoices so customers can audit rounding impact.
- For pilot/PO approvals we can provide a reconciled sample invoice for a 30-day window using your logs.

Attachment: I included a sample invoice extract that shows line-items (raw tokens, rounded tokens, quantum, applied minimum). Let us know which level of granularity procurement needs.

If helpful, Karthik can propose a small pilot credit to offset rounding noise while you evaluate KV reuse. Karthik — can you propose a simple concession (pilot credits or a temporary quantum reduction) we can offer Acme?

Best,
Chloe
